short of canning, is vacuum packing. love my vac-sealer.

I did a few tomatoes last summer (Southern Hemisphere time). They turned out great and smell and taste like fresh picked tomatoes when you open them up. Very occasionally there is a little oxidation on the top surface, can discard the oxidised ones if you want. I use the Fowler system (similar to the Ball Jars that are more common in the US afaik). Do most of mine in 20oz (Fowler #20) jars, since that is a convenient size for when I use them.

Process is pretty simple, cut up tomatoes (mine were all mini tomatoes, so only needed to halve them). Pack them into the jars and periodically squish them a bit so the juice is just level with the top. Try to get rid of as many air bubbles as you can. Then they went into the preserver submerged to almost the top of the jar in cold water and the preserver run for 1hr, leave to cool a bit then fish them out.

If you are successful, the lids will have a good suction seal, if the seal breaks they're no good. Did 18 jars and had no dodgy seals, so it's fairly reliable if you pay attention to ensure the seal ring is seated correctly and clean before putting on the lid.
